title: Existence of a flat stage in a filtered colimit
statement: Intermediate theorem used in the decomposition of lem-weil-pbc-colimit-flat-ring-map.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 02JO (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat, algebra.tex line 47331), part (3), applied to the system $(R_\lambda\to S_\lambda,M_\lambda)=(B_i\to C_i,C_i)_{i\ge0}$; this is the algebra result stated in the proof of Limits, Lemma Tag 04AI (lemma-descend-flat-finite-presentation, limits.tex line 1868), second paragraph

proof.text: *Step 1 (the systems $B_i$, $C_i$).* Work over the directed set $I'=\{i\in I:i\ge0\}$ and write $\beta_i:B_i\to B$, $\gamma_i:C_i\to C$ for the maps $\alpha_i\otimes\mathrm{id}$ ($\alpha_i:A_i\to A$ the coprojections) and $\beta_{ji},\gamma_{ji}$ ($i\le j$) for the transition maps; they are ring maps and $\varphi\circ\beta_i=\gamma_i\circ\varphi_i$, $\varphi_j\circ\beta_{ji}=\gamma_{ji}\circ\varphi_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise] (with $M_0=B_0$, resp. $C_0$) every element of $B$ is some $\beta_i(t)$, and $\beta_i(t)=0$ implies $\beta_{ji}(t)=0$ for some $j\ge i$; likewise for $C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-criterion] ($I'$ as a filtered category, $\mathbf Z$-modules) $B$ is the colimit of the abelian groups $B_i$; for a cocone of ring maps $g_i:B_i\to T$ the induced additive $g:B\to T$ is multiplicative and unital, because any two elements of $B$ come from one $B_i$ ($I'$ directed) where $g_i$ is a ring map. So $(B,(\beta_i))$ is the colimit of the rings $B_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and $(C,(\gamma_i))$ that of the $C_i$. Since $C_0$ is a $B_0$-algebra via $\varphi_0$, associativity of $\otimes$ gives isomorphisms of $B$-, resp. $B_i$-algebras $C=A\otimes_{A_0}C_0\cong B\otimes_{B_0}C_0$ and $C_i\cong B_i\otimes_{B_0}C_0$, under which $\varphi$, $\varphi_i$ become $b\mapsto b\otimes1$; hence $\varphi$ and every $\varphi_i$ are of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] (1) [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and for $i\le j$ (also with $B,C$ in place of $B_j,C_j$) $B_j\otimes_{B_i}C_i\cong B_j\otimes_{B_0}C_0\cong C_j$, $b\otimes c\mapsto\varphi_j(b)\gamma_{ji}(c)$, an isomorphism of $B_j$-algebras.

source.place: Lemma Tag 02JO (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat, line 47331), hypotheses (a)-(c) of part (3) for the system $(B_i\to C_i,C_i)$

proof.text: *Step 2 (Noetherian approximation of $\varphi$).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-finite-presentation] to $\varphi:B\to C$ (finitely presented by step 1): a nonempty directed set $\Lambda$, ring maps $\rho_\lambda:P_\lambda\to Q_\lambda$ (its $R_\lambda\to S_\lambda$), coprojections $\pi_\lambda:P_\lambda\to B$, $\kappa_\lambda:Q_\lambda\to C$ with $\varphi\pi_\lambda=\kappa_\lambda\rho_\lambda$, satisfying its (1)-(5). $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian (every ideal is principal) [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; so each $P_\lambda$, a finite type $\mathbf Z$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and of finite presentation over $\mathbf Z$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]; each $Q_\lambda$ is of finite type over the Noetherian ring $P_\lambda$, hence Noetherian and of finite presentation over $P_\lambda$ by the same two nodes. (Stacks uses the system of Lemma 00R1 for $(R\to S,M)$; here $M=S=C$ and the system of 00R0 with $M_\lambda=Q_\lambda$ serves.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 02JO (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat, line 47331), proof of (1), first sentence

proof.text: *Step 3 (the flat loci $U_\lambda$; persistence).* For $\lambda\in\Lambda$ let $U_\lambda=\{\mathfrak q'\in\operatorname{Spec}Q_\lambda:(Q_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q'}\text{ is a flat }P_\lambda\text{-module}\}$; it is open by [lem-weil-pbc-openness-of-flatness] ($P_\lambda\to Q_\lambda$ of finite presentation by step 2, $M=Q_\lambda=\operatorname{coker}(0\to Q_\lambda)$). Claim: for $\lambda\le\mu$ and $\mathfrak q'\in\operatorname{Spec}Q_\mu$ whose inverse image $\mathfrak q''$ in $Q_\lambda$ lies in $U_\lambda$, $\mathfrak q'\in U_\mu$. Proof: let $T=Q_\lambda\setminus\mathfrak q''$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] ($A=M=Q_\lambda$, $R=P_\lambda$, $N=P_\mu$) the localization of $Q_\lambda\otimes_{P_\lambda}P_\mu$ at $T$ is $(Q_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q''}\otimes_{P_\lambda}P_\mu$, which is a flat $P_\mu$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]; by clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-finite-presentation] $Q_\lambda\otimes_{P_\lambda}P_\mu\cong Q_\mu$, so $T^{-1}Q_\mu$ (localization at the image of $T$) is a flat $P_\mu$-algebra. The image of $T$ lies in $Q_\mu\setminus\mathfrak q'$, so $(Q_\mu)_{\mathfrak q'}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is the localization of $T^{-1}Q_\mu$ at the image of $Q_\mu\setminus\mathfrak q'$ (conditions (a)-(c) of a localization are checked directly), a flat ring map by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]; so $P_\mu\to(Q_\mu)_{\mathfrak q'}$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp].

source.place: Lemma Tag 02JO (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat, line 47331), proof of (1), second paragraph ('By Theorem 00RC we get an open subset $U_\lambda$'); the persistence 'for all $\lambda\ge\lambda_{\mathfrak q}$', asserted there, is the claim

proof.text: *Step 4 (each prime of $C$ lies in the flat locus of some stage).* Let $\mathfrak q\subset C$ be prime, $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, $\mathfrak q_\lambda=\kappa_\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, $\mathfrak p_\lambda=\pi_\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak p)=\rho_\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q_\lambda)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-localization-at-prime] the localizations $(P_\lambda)_{\mathfrak p_\lambda}$, $(Q_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q_\lambda}$ form directed systems of rings with colimits $B_{\mathfrak p}$, $C_{\mathfrak q}$, and the transition maps are local (its clause (1)). Take in [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-eventually-flat] its $A_\lambda=(P_\lambda)_{\mathfrak p_\lambda}$, $B_\lambda=N_\lambda=(Q_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q_\lambda}$. Its hypotheses: these are Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] local rings [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; $(P_\lambda)_{\mathfrak p_\lambda}\to(Q_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q_\lambda}$ is local as $\rho_\lambda(\mathfrak p_\lambda)\subseteq\mathfrak q_\lambda$; $N_\lambda$ is generated by $1$; (b) holds as $N_\lambda\otimes_{B_\lambda}B_\mu=B_\mu$. For (a): by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] (identity maps, which are localizations at $P_\lambda\setminus\mathfrak p_\lambda$ since that set acts bijectively on both factors) $(Q_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q_\lambda}\otimes_{(P_\lambda)_{\mathfrak p_\lambda}}(P_\mu)_{\mathfrak p_\mu}=(Q_\lambda)_{\mathfrak q_\lambda}\otimes_{P_\lambda}(P_\mu)_{\mathfrak p_\mu}$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base], applied in each factor, this is the localization of $Q_\lambda\otimes_{P_\lambda}P_\mu\cong Q_\mu$ ([lem-weil-pbc-limit-finite-presentation] (4)) at the multiplicative set $W$ generated by the images of $Q_\lambda\setminus\mathfrak q_\lambda$ and $P_\mu\setminus\mathfrak p_\mu$; $W\subseteq Q_\mu\setminus\mathfrak q_\mu$, so $(Q_\mu)_{\mathfrak q_\mu}$ is the localization of $W^{-1}Q_\mu$ at the image of $Q_\mu\setminus\mathfrak q_\mu$, and the composite is the map of (a), a localization of the tensor product. The colimit of the abelian groups $N_\lambda$ is $C_{\mathfrak q}$ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-underlying-module] ($R=\mathbf Z$), and $C_{\mathfrak q}$ is a flat $B_{\mathfrak p}$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps], $\varphi$ being flat. So some $(Q_{\lambda_{\mathfrak q}})_{\mathfrak q_{\lambda_{\mathfrak q}}}$ is flat over $(P_{\lambda_{\mathfrak q}})_{\mathfrak p_{\lambda_{\mathfrak q}}}$, hence over $P_{\lambda_{\mathfrak q}}$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization]: $\mathfrak q_{\lambda_{\mathfrak q}}\in U_{\lambda_{\mathfrak q}}$. As $\mathfrak q_\lambda$ is the inverse image of $\mathfrak q_\mu$ for $\lambda\le\mu$, step 3 gives $\mathfrak q_\mu\in U_\mu$ for all $\mu\ge\lambda_{\mathfrak q}$.

proof.text: *Step 5 (quasi-compactness: one stage covers $\operatorname{Spec}C$).* For $\lambda\in\Lambda$ let $V_\lambda=\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}C:\kappa_\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q)\in U_\lambda\}$. It is open in the Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum]: a prime of $C$ contains $\kappa_\lambda(J)$ iff its inverse image contains $J$, so the preimage of a closed set $V(J)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}Q_\lambda$ is $V(\kappa_\lambda(J)C)$. For $\lambda\le\mu$, $V_\lambda\subseteq V_\mu$ by step 3 (the inverse image in $Q_\lambda$ of $\kappa_\mu^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ is $\kappa_\lambda^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$), and $\bigcup_\lambda V_\lambda=\operatorname{Spec}C$ by step 4. $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] (iii), so finitely many $V_{\lambda_1},\dots,V_{\lambda_r}$ cover it; $\Lambda$ being nonempty and directed, there is $\lambda_0\ge\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_r$, and $V_{\lambda_0}=\operatorname{Spec}C$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 02JO (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat, line 47331), proof of (1), second paragraph ('Since Spec(S) is quasi-compact ...')

proof.text: *Step 6 (a stage where the flat locus is everything).* The complement of the open $U_{\lambda_0}$ is $V(J)$ for an ideal $J\subseteq Q_{\lambda_0}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $C$, $\kappa_{\lambda_0}^{-1}(\mathfrak q)\in U_{\lambda_0}$ (step 5) does not contain $J$, so $\mathfrak q\in D(\kappa_{\lambda_0}(f))$ for some $f\in J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] (i) the $\kappa_{\lambda_0}(f)$, $f\in J$, generate the unit ideal: $1=\sum_{k=1}^r\kappa_{\lambda_0}(f_k)c_k$ with $f_k\in J$, $c_k\in C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (2) ($R=\mathbf Z$) and directedness there are $\lambda_1\ge\lambda_0$ and $d_k\in Q_{\lambda_1}$ with $\kappa_{\lambda_1}(d_k)=c_k$; the element $\sum_k\bar f_kd_k-1$ of $Q_{\lambda_1}$ maps to $0$ in $C$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero] it maps to $0$ in some $Q_{\lambda'}$, $\lambda'\ge\lambda_1$: $\sum_k\bar f_k\bar d_k=1$ in $Q_{\lambda'}$. Let $\mathfrak q'\in\operatorname{Spec}Q_{\lambda'}$. Some $\bar f_k\notin\mathfrak q'$, so the inverse image of $\mathfrak q'$ in $Q_{\lambda_0}$ does not contain $f_k\in J$, i.e. lies in $U_{\lambda_0}$; by step 3, $\mathfrak q'\in U_{\lambda'}$. Hence $U_{\lambda'}=\operatorname{Spec}Q_{\lambda'}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 02JO (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat, line 47331), proof of (1), third paragraph

proof.text: *Step 7 (a flat Noetherian model).* Put $P'=P_{\lambda'}$, $Q'=Q_{\lambda'}$, $\rho'=\rho_{\lambda'}$. For every prime $\mathfrak q'$ of $Q'$, with $\mathfrak p'=\rho'^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$, $(Q')_{\mathfrak q'}$ is a flat $P'$-module (step 6), hence a flat $P'_{\mathfrak p'}$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] (it is a $P'_{\mathfrak p'}$-module, the elements of $P'\setminus\mathfrak p'$ mapping outside $\mathfrak q'$). By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-map-local-criterion], $\rho':P'\to Q'$ is flat. Recall (step 2) $P'$ is of finite presentation over $\mathbf Z$, $Q'$ of finite presentation over $P'$, and by clause (5) of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-finite-presentation] $\theta:Q'\otimes_{P'}B\to C$, $q\otimes b\mapsto\kappa_{\lambda'}(q)\varphi(b)$, is an isomorphism of $B$-algebras ($B$ a $P'$-algebra via $\pi_{\lambda'}$).

proof.text: Tensor base change of the flat Noetherian model gives flatness of the stage map at the index obtained in step 8; this proves existence of a flat stage. No persistence assertion is needed here.
